<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video, scored mostly in rests.</b><br>
  <sub>working title · in development, nothing published yet · an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i></sub>
</p>

**Castaway** is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft, a pair of cream headphones and a great deal of time. She sits in the shade and nods to the music. Every so often, always on the next bar, something happens. A bottle she throws washes straight back to her feet. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the crab walks off wearing it. Then she goes back to nodding, which is the main event. Sunny and hand-painted, 16:9, 1080p at 30 fps, and always daytime.

The screen up there is one minute of it, written out as a module. Channels 0 to 3 are the theme. Channels 4 to 7 are the island, and they are mostly dots, because the island is mostly waiting. This minute, a shark in headphones circles for nine bars, surfaces, and nods along with her on every beat for six more. The cat sleeps through it in the palm. The turtle is elsewhere. The ocean plays one note at 00:00:00 and leaves it running for the rest of the minute. Somebody keeps clicking Nod.

[activities.toml](activities.toml) is the instrument list: more than 90 activities, each on one of four timers. Regular ones come round every 2 to 5 minutes, occasional every 12 to 25, rare every 30 to 60, and super rare every 3 to 6 hours, three at most per run. In a typical ten-hour run (the median of 200 simulated ones) that comes to about 155 regular, 30 occasional, 13 rare and 2 super-rare events, plus chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time. The other two thirds are the dots.

Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies, and the sample list is a list of things arithmetic made. The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major (ii-V-I-vi), 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean is another seamless minute, and there are more than 150 sound files in all. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the levels can be set for the master and per routine. Nobody has listened to any of it yet. The scopes are drawn, not measured, so they have no opinion either.

```sh
python tools/serve.py               # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py            # validate the schedule, simulate 10 hours
python tools/render_demo.py --dev   # a dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

<sub>The page at <a href="web/index.html">web/index.html</a> previews live and exports a YouTube-ready MP4: frame-exact H.264 encoded in the browser with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes in the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. <code>render_demo.py</code> is the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, and the default run is 10:00:00 on seed 1992: same seed, same video.</sub>

<details>
<summary><b>Help</b>: how to read the screen</summary>

```text
 HELP: HOW TO READ THE SCREEN                          one loop = one minute
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 BPM 080  Spd. 06   the theme's tempo. at speed 6 a row lasts 0.1875 s, so
                    16 rows make one bar of exactly 3 seconds
 Ln. 040            64 rows to a pattern (hex, like everything here): 4 bars
 Songlen. 05        5 patterns, 20 bars, 60 seconds: the whole theme loop
 Repstart 00        then round again. ten hours is 600 laps
 Time 00:00:44      where we are in the loop. it wraps when the theme does
 Avail. all day     she is
 Signal 0 bars      there is one bar. it is at the top of the palm
 rows 00 10 20 30   bar lines, in white. every activity starts on one
 ch 0 1 2           keys, kalimba, drums: invented notes on the real bar
                    map. keys alone, drums from bar 2, kalimba from bar 6,
                    the whole tune in bars 10 to 15, kick and rim to finish
 ch 3  ocean        one note. the rest of the minute is the loop
 ch 4  her          dots mean idle, and idle is the default
 ch 5  cat          asleep in the palm. dots
 ch 6  turtle       not here this minute. dots
 ch 7  sea+sky      a shark in headphones, start to finish
 ===                the lane goes quiet
 A0F                volume slides down: the shark sinks
 7A-7F              the theme's own instruments, at the far end of bank two
 Nibbles            fishing. nibbles, nothing, the usual
 Zzz                the cat's button
 Nod                clicked on every beat. not while she freezes
 Wait, Wait more,   the three speeds of the island
 Adv. Wait
```

```text
 PTN. 00-04: THIS MINUTE, BAR BY BAR         shark_nod, each step inside its
                                             range in activities.toml
 bars  0-8   ch 7     a fin circles the island ...................... 27 s
 bar   9     ch 4     she notices, and freezes ....................... 3 s
 bar  10     ch 7     it surfaces: headphones ........................ 3 s
 bars 11-16  ch 4+7   they nod to the beat, a note per beat each .... 18 s
 bar  17     ch 4+7   a last nod, and it sinks ....................... 3 s
 bars 18-19  ch 4     back to the music .............................. 6 s
                                                              total   60 s
```

No ship this minute. The sea lane was taken.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Instr. Ed.</b>: bank one, and what is further down the list</summary>

```text
 INSTR. ED.   bank one of two                       more than 90 activities
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 ##  instrument              lanes      timer       what happens
 01  coconut sip             her        regular     shade, coconut, eyes shut
 02  fishing (nibbles only)  her        regular     nibbles. nothing. usual
 03  bottle, thrown back     her        occasional  it washes straight back
 04  delivery drone          sea, her   rare        the parcel: headphones
 05  shark in headphones     sea, her   rare        it nods on the beat
 06  sea turtle visit        turtle,    occasional  it crawls up; they both
                             her                    doze off
 07  stray cat, by crate     cat        rare        climbs the palm, naps,
                                                    floats off one day
 08  ship nobody sees        sea        occasional  sails past while she is
                                                    busy. it waits for that

 Swap Bank, and further down the list:
     sandcastle                         regular     the tide takes it, later
     jogging laps                       regular     there and back. small
     coconut and hermit crab            occasional  the crab walks off in it
     kumara                             occasional  planted; grows all video
     signal hunt                        rare        one bar, top of the palm
     tour boat                          rare        selfies. no lift offered
     e-foil bro                         rare        a wave, a shaka, gone
     bushcraft                          rare        fire by friction, a
                                                    hammock, a lookout,
                                                    spear fishing
     bottle reply                       chained     a different bottle
     waving for rescue                  super rare  a ship. it toots back
     leave any time                     super rare  walks off over the
                                                    water, comes back with
                                                    an iced coffee
```

Lanes let things overlap: the sea and sky have a lane of their own, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and it will wait until she is. Every start snaps to the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so the gags land on the beat. The file listed 94 activities on 2026-10-01 and grows every few hours.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>About</b>: the easter egg, the credits and the greetings</summary>

<p align="center">
  <img src="assets/39-dos-gui-tracker_opus_5.5-about.svg" width="100%" alt="The tracker's About screen. On the left, a daylight pixel picture of the island: blue sky in stepped bands, a pale sun, small clouds drifting left, and a calm blue sea with glints that swap on the beat. One tall, slender palm with a segmented reddish-tan trunk leans over the sand, a grey tabby cat asleep in its fronds with a small z rising. In the palm's shade a young woman with brown hair and cream headphones, in a coral tank top and cream shorts, sits and nods on every beat. A small log raft is pulled up on the shore, and now and then a grey fin wearing a cream headband crosses the far water. On the right, a credits box with the Castaway wordmark reads: an island, a palm, a raft, and ten hours. she nods. now and then, always on the beat, something happens. then she nods. Below it: patterns, plate, pixels: Fermata. sound: code, all of it. daylight: all of it. rests: most of it. An Exit button sits in the corner.">
</p>

Patterns, plate and pixels by **Fermata**, who does not exist. A fermata is the sign over a note that says hold it as long as you like, which is the whole plan.

Greetings, on the beat, to the shark, for perfect timing; the cat, for sleeping through it; the turtle, for taking the minute off; the hermit crab and its new coconut; the bottle that came back; the drone and its spare headphones; the e-foil bro; and the ship, which would have been in this pattern, but the sea lane was busy.

<sub>Fermata and its tracker do not exist. The screen is drawn in the manner of mid-1990s DOS GUI trackers, and no real tracker's name, logo or screen is reproduced. The notes on channels 0 to 2 are invented; the tempo, the bar map, the routine's durations and the file names are the project's own. Castaway is an unofficial remake inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i> (1992), which belongs to its owners.</sub>

</details>
